details.availability: Weights for OpenJev-1.7B, 4B (v0.2) and 8B and the OpenJev-Data dataset are on the Hugging Face Hub; training, evaluation and serving code is on GitHub and PyPI (wev-ai, openjev-ai).

weights.reason: All three Hub model cards declare apache-2.0 (OpenJev-4B at 3687132, OpenJev-8B at 32bc7cb, OpenJev-1.7B at 7418ae8). This covers the released weights only; the README warns that parts of the training data are research-only or subject to a model provider's terms.

details.training_data_note: Publisher-listed sources: Mind2Web and NNetNav-live browser steps (NNetNav stop labels relabelled by an LLM judge), judge-verified teacher episodes from jev-ultrafast runs on live sites with qwen3-max and later GLM-5.3-Flash as System One, and general typed-decision corpora (Kev decision-v7, typed-decisions, tasksource-jev, jev-distill, typed-decisions-synth). The README warns that some tasksource-jev tasks are research-only and that teacher episodes are model outputs under their provider's terms.

weights.basis: Publisher model cards for OpenJev-1.7B, 4B and 8B each declare apache-2.0 in their metadata headers; the README notes that some training data carries its own terms.

name: OpenJev
notes: Models and code for an open replacement of a hosted System One decision API. A Qwen3 or Qwen3.5 backbone without its vocabulary head scores each option with a pointer head, so one pass answers every question in a request; a local server exposes POST /v1/systemone. Browser steps arrive as page text, numbered elements and recent actions, and the model chooses an operation (click, type, DONE and others) and a target element. The repository holds the wev package (data conversion for Mind2Web, NNetNav and WebChain, training, calibration, export, serving), teacher-collection scripts, the OpenJev-Bench browser-lane client (2,346 frozen steps stored in the Hub dataset alanhuangya/OpenJev-Data), locked results and the paper source; the paper is a Zenodo deposit (doi 10.5281/zenodo.22941164) with no catalog record. The models also answer general decisions such as triage and routing. Results are publisher-reported, and live-website numbers use an LLM judge.
summary: Decision models at 1.7B, 4B and 8B that answer typed questions with calibrated probabilities in one pass; trained on browser-agent steps and general decision data, they pick a web agent's next operation and element.
